decisions.choice: an oracle: a solemn message from God
decisions.reason: The word comes from the verb "lift up", and is used for a message the prophet lifts up his voice to deliver. Older translations rendered it "burden". It heads Zechariah 9:1 and 12:1 in the same way: "An oracle: the word of the LORD". |

decisions.choice: Malachi: the prophet's name, which means "my messenger"
alternatives: "my messenger", as a title rather than a name
decisions.reason: The name means "my messenger", the same word the LORD uses in 3:1 ("I am sending my messenger"). Nothing else is known of the prophet, and some think the word here is a title drawn from 3:1, not a personal name. The Greek translation is generally said to read "by the hand of his messenger", and the Aramaic Targum adds "whose name is called Ezra the scribe". The book is read here as the words of a prophet named Malachi.

decisions.choice: the time of Malachi: after the temple was rebuilt, in the Persian period
decisions.reason: The temple is standing and sacrifices are offered (1:10; 3:1, 10), and a governor rules (1:8), so the book comes from after 515 BC. Its concerns, careless priests, marriage to foreign wives, and tithes withheld, are those Ezra and Nehemiah dealt with in the middle of the fifth century BC (Ezra 9-10; Nehemiah 13), so it is usually dated near their time. |

decisions.choice: the word of the LORD to Israel: a series of disputes
decisions.reason: The book is built of six disputes (1:2-5; 1:6-2:9; 2:10-16; 2:17-3:5; 3:6-12; 3:13-21), each following one pattern: the LORD makes a statement, the people object, "But you say, ...?", and the LORD answers. "Israel" here is the whole people of God living in Judah after the exile. |

decisions.choice: oracle (L, B), message (R); the disputes set in lines
decisions.reason: Massa' follows the Isaiah table. Malachi is close to prose, but it is a prophet's oracle and its verses divide clearly at the Hebrew accents, so it is set in lines at every level, breaking at the main accent and, where a verse is long, at the lesser ones. The people's questions are set in double quotes and the LORD's words have none, as in Isaiah. |

decisions.choice: I have loved you: the LORD's covenant love, by which he chose his people
decisions.reason: The love meant here is the LORD's choice of Israel and his faithfulness to that choice. "It was not because you were more numerous than any other people that the LORD set his love on you ... but because the LORD loved you" (Deuteronomy 7:7-8). The book begins with this love before any rebuke. |

decisions.choice: But you say, "How have you loved us?": the pattern of the disputes
decisions.reason: The people answer every statement of the LORD with a question that challenges it (1:6, 7; 2:14, 17; 3:7, 8, 13). Here they doubt that he loves them at all, after years of hardship. The questions are quoted words of the people. |

decisions.choice: Esau and Jacob: the ancestors of Edom and Israel
decisions.reason: Esau and Jacob were twin sons of Isaac; Esau's descendants became the people of Edom, south-east of Judah, and Jacob's became Israel (Genesis 25:23-30; 36:1). Though they were brothers, the LORD chose Jacob, the younger. |

decisions.choice: And I loved Jacob (L), Even so, I loved Jacob (B); Yet I chose to love Jacob (R)
decisions.reason: With the first words of verse 3, the line reads "I loved Jacob, but Esau I hated" (L, B) and "I chose to love Jacob, but I rejected Esau" (R), the wording published in Romans 9:13. The LORD's question "How have you loved us?" uses the deity_pronoun setting, because the people speak to him. |

God speaks to the people in the plural, so every "you" takes plural_you. The people's "you" to God is in the verb only ("has amado"), so the deity_pronoun span goes only where a free pronoun stands (R "tu amor").

decisions.choice: I loved Jacob, but Esau I hated: I chose Jacob, and did not choose Esau
decisions.reason: In Hebrew, "love" and "hate" set side by side often mean preferring one and setting the other aside, not the feelings the words usually name. Jacob "loved" Rachel and "hated" Leah, meaning he loved her less (Genesis 29:30-31); Deuteronomy 21:15 speaks of a loved wife and a "hated" one. Jesus' saying that his followers must "hate" their families (Luke 14:26) is given in Matthew 10:37 as loving them "more than me". Here the LORD chose Jacob to be his people and did not choose Esau.

decisions.choice: quoted in Romans 9:13
decisions.reason: Paul quotes "Jacob I loved, but Esau I hated" in Romans 9:13 to show that God's choice rests on his own purpose, not on what people do. |

decisions.choice: his mountains a desolation: the ruin of Edom
decisions.reason: Edom's land was the hill country of Seir, south-east of the Dead Sea. After the fall of Jerusalem, Edom itself was overrun, by the Babylonian king Nabonidus in the 550s BC and then by Arab peoples moving in from the desert, who later became the Nabateans. By Malachi's day its towns lay in ruins. |

decisions.reason: The term sheet's wording, as the published Romans 9:13 R; the idiom (choosing and not choosing) is in the English footnote.

source.text: כִּֽי־תֹאמַ֨ר אֱד֜וֹם רֻשַּׁ֗שְׁנוּ וְנָשׁוּב֙ וְנִבְנֶ֣ה חֳרָב֔וֹת כֹּ֤ה אָמַר֙ יְהוָ֣ה צְבָא֔וֹת הֵ֥מָּה יִבְנ֖וּ וַאֲנִ֣י אֶהֱר֑וֹס וְקָרְא֤וּ לָהֶם֙ גְּב֣וּל רִשְׁעָ֔ה וְהָעָ֛ם אֲשֶׁר־זָעַ֥ם יְהוָ֖ה עַד־עוֹלָֽם׃

records.literal_gloss: Though Edom says, We have been shattered, but we will return and build [the] ruins, thus says Yahweh of hosts: They will build, but I will tear down; and they will be called [the] territory of wickedness, and the people with whom Yahweh is indignant forever.

en.L: If Edom says, "We have been shattered, but we will return and build the ruins," \q thus says {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} of hosts: They will build, but I will tear down; \q and they will be called the territory of wickedness, \q and the people with whom {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} is indignant forever.
en.B: Edom may say, "We have been crushed, but we will rebuild the ruins." \q But {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} of Armies says this: They may build, but I will tear down. \q They will be called the Land of Wickedness, \q the people with whom {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} is angry forever.
en.R: The people of Edom may say, "Our towns have been destroyed, but we will build them again." \q But this is what {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} of Armies says: They can build, but I will tear it all down. \q People will call their country the Land of Evil, \q and they will be known as the people {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} is always angry with.

fr.L: Si Édom dit : « Nous avons été écrasés, mais nous reviendrons et nous rebâtirons les ruines », \q ainsi parle {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} des armées : Eux, ils bâtiront, mais moi, je démolirai ; \q et on les appellera territoire de la méchanceté, \q et le peuple contre lequel {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} est irrité pour toujours.
fr.B: Édom peut bien dire : « Nous avons été écrasés, mais nous rebâtirons les ruines. » \q {{divine_name:Le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} des armées dit ceci : Qu’ils bâtissent, moi je démolirai. \q On les appellera Pays de la méchanceté, \q le peuple contre qui {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} est irrité pour toujours.
fr.R: Les habitants d’Édom diront peut-être : « Nos villes ont été détruites, mais nous allons les reconstruire. » \q Mais voici ce que dit {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} des armées : Ils peuvent construire, mais moi, je démolirai tout. \q On appellera leur pays le Pays du mal, \q et on dira d’eux : « C’est le peuple contre qui {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} est toujours en colère. »

es.L: Si Edom dice: «Hemos sido destruidos, pero volveremos a edificar las ruinas», \q así dice {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} de los ejércitos: Ellos edificarán, pero yo derribaré; \q y los llamarán territorio de maldad, \q y pueblo contra el cual {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} está indignado para siempre.
es.B: Edom podrá decir: «Hemos sido aplastados, pero reconstruiremos las ruinas». \q Pero {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} de los Ejércitos dice esto: Ellos podrán edificar, pero yo derribaré. \q Los llamarán Tierra de Maldad, \q el pueblo contra el cual {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} está enojado para siempre.
es.R: La gente de Edom podrá decir: «Nuestras ciudades han sido destruidas, pero las volveremos a construir». \q Pero esto es lo que dice {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} de los Ejércitos: Ellos podrán construir, pero yo lo derribaré todo. \q La gente llamará a su país la Tierra de la Maldad, \q y serán conocidos como el pueblo con el que {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} está siempre enojado.

vi.L: Nếu Ê-đôm nói: "Chúng tôi đã bị đập tan, nhưng chúng tôi sẽ trở lại xây dựng những nơi đổ nát," \q thì {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} Vạn Quân phán thế này: Chúng xây, nhưng {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} sẽ phá đổ; \q chúng sẽ được gọi là lãnh thổ của sự gian ác, \q và dân mà {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} giận đời đời.
vi.B: Ê-đôm có thể nói: "Chúng tôi đã bị nghiền nát, nhưng chúng tôi sẽ xây lại những nơi đổ nát." \q Nhưng {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} Vạn Quân phán như vầy: Chúng cứ xây, nhưng {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} sẽ phá đổ. \q Người ta sẽ gọi chúng là Xứ Gian Ác, \q là dân mà {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} giận đời đời.
vi.R: Dân Ê-đôm có thể nói: "Các thành của chúng tôi đã bị tàn phá, nhưng chúng tôi sẽ xây lại." \q Nhưng đây là lời {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} Vạn Quân phán: Chúng cứ xây, nhưng {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} sẽ phá đổ tất cả. \q Người ta sẽ gọi xứ chúng là Xứ Gian Ác, \q và biết chúng là dân mà {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} luôn luôn giận.

sw.L: Ikiwa Edomu atasema, "Tumevunjwa, lakini tutarudi na kujenga magofu," \q {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} wa majeshi asema hivi: Wao watajenga, lakini mimi nitabomoa; \q nao wataitwa nchi ya uovu, \q na watu ambao {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} amewakasirikia milele.
sw.B: Edomu anaweza kusema, "Tumepondwa, lakini tutayajenga upya magofu." \q Lakini hivi ndivyo {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} wa majeshi asemavyo: Wanaweza kujenga, lakini mimi nitabomoa. \q Wataitwa Nchi ya Uovu, \q watu ambao {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} amewakasirikia milele.
sw.R: Watu wa Edomu wanaweza kusema, "Miji yetu imeharibiwa, lakini tutaijenga tena." \q Lakini hili ndilo {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} wa majeshi analosema: Wanaweza kujenga, lakini nitabomoa vyote. \q Watu wataiita nchi yao Nchi ya Uovu, \q nao watajulikana kama watu ambao {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} huwakasirikia siku zote.

ko.L: 에돔이 "우리가 부서졌으나, 돌아가서 무너진 곳들을 다시 세우겠다" 하고 말하여도, \q 만군의 {{divine_name:주|야훼}}께서 이와 같이 말씀하신다. 그들은 세우겠지만 나는 허물겠다. \q 사람들이 그들을 '악의 땅', \q '{{divine_name:주|야훼}}가 영원히 진노하는 백성'이라 부를 것이다.
ko.B: 에돔이 "우리가 무너졌지만, 폐허를 다시 세우겠다" 하고 말할지라도, \q 만군의 {{divine_name:주|야훼}}께서 이렇게 말씀하신다. 그들이 세워도 나는 허물어 버리겠다. \q 사람들이 그들을 '악한 땅'이라 부르고, \q '{{divine_name:주|야훼}}가 영원히 진노하는 백성'이라 부를 것이다.
ko.R: 에돔 사람들이 "우리 성읍들이 무너졌지만, 우리가 다시 세우겠다" 하고 말할지도 모른다. \q 그러나 하늘의 군대를 거느리신 {{divine_name:주|야훼}}께서 하시는 말씀이다. 그들이 세워도 나는 모두 허물어 버리겠다. \q 사람들은 그 나라를 '악한 땅'이라고 부를 것이다. \q 그들은 '{{divine_name:주|야훼}}가 언제까지나 화를 내는 백성'으로 알려질 것이다.

decisions.choice: Edom's words: a boast that it will recover
decisions.reason: Edom's own words are quoted. It admits the ruin but expects to rebuild. The LORD answers that he will undo whatever it builds. |

decisions.choice: the territory of wickedness: a name that shows what they are
decisions.reason: Israel's land is called the LORD's holy land (Zechariah 2:16); Edom's will be named for its wickedness. "The people with whom the LORD is indignant" is a second such name. |

decisions.choice: indignant forever: under the LORD's lasting anger
decisions.reason: The verb means to be indignant, to denounce or curse (Numbers 23:7-8; Proverbs 24:24). Edom's fall is lasting, unlike Israel's, which the LORD reversed. |

decisions.choice: Thus says the LORD of hosts (L), The LORD of Armies says this (B), This is what the LORD of Armies says (R)
decisions.reason: The formula follows the Isaiah table. Edom's words are quoted in double quotes. Balanced and Readable write "Land of Wickedness" and "Land of Evil" with capitals as a name. |

decisions.choice: "Así dice el SEÑOR de los ejércitos:" (L); "El SEÑOR de los Ejércitos dice esto:" (B); "esto es lo que dice el SEÑOR de los Ejércitos:" (R)
decisions.reason: The messenger formula and "the LORD of hosts" follow the Spanish prophets at each level, through Malachi; Edom's words, human speech inside the oracle, take « ».

decisions.choice: "{{divine_name:주|야훼}}가 영원히 진노하는 백성" without -시-
decisions.reason: The name is part of God's own speech, so it keeps no honorific (term sheet), though the English names him in the third person. The names are set in single quotation marks.

source.text: וְעֵינֵיכֶ֖ם תִּרְאֶ֑ינָה וְאַתֶּ֤ם תֹּֽאמְרוּ֙ יִגְדַּ֣ל יְהוָ֔ה מֵעַ֖ל לִגְב֥וּל יִשְׂרָאֵֽל׃

records.literal_gloss: And your eyes will see, and you will say, Great [is] Yahweh beyond the border of Israel.

en.L: Your own eyes will see it, \q and you will say, "Great is {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} \q beyond the border of Israel!"
en.B: You will see it with your own eyes, \q and you will say, "Great is {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, \q even beyond the borders of Israel!"
en.R: You will see this for yourselves. \q Then you will say, "{{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} is great, \q even outside the land of Israel!"

fr.L: Et vos yeux [le] verront, \q et vous direz : « Grand est {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} \q au-delà de la frontière d’Israël ! »
fr.B: Vous le verrez de vos propres yeux, \q et vous direz : « {{divine_name:Le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} est grand, \q même au-delà des frontières d’Israël ! »
fr.R: Vous le verrez vous-mêmes. \q Alors vous direz : « {{divine_name:Le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} est grand, \q même en dehors du pays d’Israël ! »

es.L: Y {{plural_you:sus ojos|vuestros ojos}} [lo] verán, \q y {{plural_you:ustedes dirán|vosotros diréis}}: «¡Grande es {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} \q más allá de la frontera de Israel!».
es.B: {{plural_you:Lo verán con sus propios ojos|Lo veréis con vuestros propios ojos}}, \q y {{plural_you:dirán|diréis}}: «¡Grande es {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}}, \q aun más allá de las fronteras de Israel!».
es.R: {{plural_you:Ustedes mismos lo verán|Vosotros mismos lo veréis}}. \q Entonces {{plural_you:dirán|diréis}}: «¡{{divine_name:El SEÑOR|Yahvé}} es grande, \q aun fuera de la tierra de Israel!».

vi.L: Chính mắt các ngươi sẽ thấy, \q và các ngươi sẽ nói: "{{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} thật vĩ đại \q vượt ra ngoài bờ cõi Y-sơ-ra-ên!"
vi.B: Các ngươi sẽ thấy tận mắt, \q và các ngươi sẽ nói: "{{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} thật vĩ đại, \q vượt cả ra ngoài bờ cõi Y-sơ-ra-ên!"
vi.R: Các ngươi sẽ tự mắt mình thấy điều đó. \q Bấy giờ các ngươi sẽ nói: "{{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} thật vĩ đại, \q ngay cả bên ngoài đất Y-sơ-ra-ên!"

sw.L: Na macho yenu wenyewe yataona, \q nanyi mtasema, "{{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} ni mkuu \q hata nje ya mpaka wa Israeli!"
sw.B: Mtaona hayo kwa macho yenu wenyewe, \q nanyi mtasema, "{{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} ni mkuu, \q hata nje ya mipaka ya Israeli!"
sw.R: Mtajionea wenyewe. \q Ndipo mtasema, "{{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} ni mkuu, \q hata nje ya nchi ya Israeli!"

ko.L: 너희 눈이 그것을 볼 것이고, \q 너희가 "{{divine_name:주|야훼}}께서는 이스라엘 국경 밖에서도 \q 위대하시다!" 하고 말할 것이다.
ko.B: 너희는 너희 눈으로 그것을 보고, \q "{{divine_name:주|야훼}}께서는 위대하시다. \q 이스라엘 국경 너머에서도 위대하시다!" 하고 말할 것이다.
ko.R: 너희는 그것을 직접 보게 될 것이다. \q 그러면 너희가 "{{divine_name:주|야훼}}께서는 위대하신 분이다. \q 이스라엘 땅 밖에서도 위대하시다!" 하고 말할 것이다.

decisions.choice: beyond the border of Israel: the LORD's greatness reaches past Israel's land
decisions.reason: The words can mean "above" or "beyond" the border. Most take them as "beyond": the LORD's rule is seen in what he does to Edom, outside Israel. Read the other way, the people praise him for what he does over Israel's own land.

decisions.choice: you will say: the doubters of verse 2 will praise
decisions.reason: Those who asked "How have you loved us?" will answer their own question when they see what happens to Edom. |

decisions.choice: the people's words in double quotes
decisions.reason: The people's words of praise are quoted, as their questions are. |

source.text: בֵּ֛ן יְכַבֵּ֥ד אָ֖ב וְעֶ֣בֶד אֲדֹנָ֑יו וְאִם־אָ֣ב אָ֣נִי אַיֵּ֣ה כְבוֹדִ֡י וְאִם־אֲדוֹנִ֣ים אָנִי֩ אַיֵּ֨ה מוֹרָאִ֜י אָמַ֣ר׀יְהוָ֣ה צְבָא֗וֹת לָכֶם֙ הַכֹּֽהֲנִים֙ בּוֹזֵ֣י שְׁמִ֔י וַאֲמַרְתֶּ֕ם בַּמֶּ֥ה בָזִ֖ינוּ אֶת־שְׁמֶֽךָ׃

records.literal_gloss: A son honors [his] father, and a slave his master. And if I [am] a father, where [is] my honor? And if I [am] a master, where [is] my fear? says Yahweh of hosts to you, the priests, despisers of my name. And you say, In what have we despised your name?

en.L: A son honors [his] father, and a slave his master. \q And if a father [am] I, where [is] {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} honor? And if a master [am] I, where [is] the fear of {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}? says {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} of hosts to you, O priests, who despise {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} name. \q But you say, "How have we despised {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} name?"
en.B: A son honors his father, and a servant honors his master. \q If I am a father, where is the honor due to {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}? If I am a master, where is the respect due to {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}? says {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} of Armies to you priests who despise {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} name. \q Yet you ask, "In what way have we despised {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} name?"
en.R: A son honors his father, and a servant respects his master. \q I am a father to you, so why do you not honor {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}? I am your master, so why do you not respect {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}? says {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} of Armies. You priests treat {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} name with contempt! \q But you ask, "How have we treated {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} name with contempt?"

fr.L: Un fils honore [son] père, et un esclave son maître. \q Et si je [suis] père, où [est] l’honneur qui {{deity_pronoun:m’|M’}}[est dû] ? Et si je [suis] maître, où [est] la crainte de {{deity_pronoun:moi|Moi}} ? dit {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} des armées, à vous, prêtres, qui méprisez {{deity_pronoun:mon|Mon}} nom. \q Mais vous dites : « En quoi avons-nous méprisé {{deity_pronoun:ton|Ton}} nom ? »
fr.B: Un fils honore son père, et un serviteur son maître. \q Si je suis père, où est l’honneur qui {{deity_pronoun:m’|M’}}est dû ? Si je suis maître, où est le respect qui {{deity_pronoun:m’|M’}}est dû ? dit {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} des armées, à vous, prêtres, qui méprisez {{deity_pronoun:mon|Mon}} nom. \q Et vous demandez : « En quoi avons-nous méprisé {{deity_pronoun:ton|Ton}} nom ? »
fr.R: Un fils honore son père, et un serviteur respecte son maître. \q Je suis un père pour vous : pourquoi ne {{deity_pronoun:m’|M’}}honorez-vous pas ? Je suis votre maître : pourquoi ne {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} respectez-vous pas ? dit {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} des armées. Vous, les prêtres, vous traitez {{deity_pronoun:mon|Mon}} nom avec mépris ! \q Mais vous dites : « Comment avons-nous traité {{deity_pronoun:ton|Ton}} nom avec mépris ? »

es.L: El hijo honra al padre, y el esclavo a su señor. \q Pues si padre soy yo, ¿dónde [está] {{deity_pronoun:mi|Mi}} honra? Y si señor soy yo, ¿dónde [está] el temor de {{deity_pronoun:mí|Mí}}?, dice {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} de los ejércitos a {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}}, oh sacerdotes, que menosprecian {{deity_pronoun:mi|Mi}} nombre. \q Pero {{plural_you:ustedes dicen|vosotros decís}}: «¿En qué hemos menospreciado {{deity_pronoun:tu|Tu}} nombre?».
es.B: El hijo honra a su padre, y el siervo honra a su señor. \q Si yo soy padre, ¿dónde está la honra que {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} deben? Si soy señor, ¿dónde está el respeto que {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} deben?, dice {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} de los Ejércitos a {{plural_you:ustedes, sacerdotes, que menosprecian|vosotros, sacerdotes, que menospreciáis}} {{deity_pronoun:mi|Mi}} nombre. \q Pero {{plural_you:ustedes preguntan|vosotros preguntáis}}: «¿De qué manera hemos menospreciado {{deity_pronoun:tu|Tu}} nombre?».
es.R: El hijo honra a su padre, y el siervo respeta a su amo. \q Yo soy un padre para {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}}; entonces, ¿por qué no {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} {{plural_you:honran|honráis}}? Yo soy {{plural_you:su amo|vuestro amo}}; entonces, ¿por qué no {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} {{plural_you:respetan|respetáis}}?, dice {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} de los Ejércitos. ¡{{plural_you:Ustedes, sacerdotes, tratan|Vosotros, sacerdotes, tratáis}} {{deity_pronoun:mi|Mi}} nombre con desprecio! \q Pero {{plural_you:ustedes preguntan|vosotros preguntáis}}: «¿Cómo hemos tratado {{deity_pronoun:tu|Tu}} nombre con desprecio?».

vi.L: Con thì tôn kính cha, và đầy tớ [tôn kính] chủ mình. \q Vậy nếu {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} là cha, thì sự tôn kính dành cho {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} ở đâu? Nếu {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} là chủ, thì sự kính sợ {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} ở đâu? {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} Vạn Quân phán với các ngươi, hỡi các thầy tế lễ, là những kẻ khinh dể danh {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}}. \q Nhưng các ngươi nói: "Chúng tôi đã khinh dể danh {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} bằng cách nào?"
vi.B: Con thì tôn kính cha, và đầy tớ tôn kính chủ mình. \q Nếu {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} là cha, thì sự tôn kính dành cho {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} ở đâu? Nếu {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} là chủ, thì sự kính trọng dành cho {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} ở đâu? {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} Vạn Quân phán với các ngươi, là các thầy tế lễ khinh dể danh {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}}. \q Thế mà các ngươi hỏi: "Chúng tôi đã khinh dể danh {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} ở chỗ nào?"
vi.R: Con thì tôn kính cha mình, và đầy tớ kính trọng chủ mình. \q Ta là cha của các ngươi, vậy sao các ngươi không tôn kính {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}}? Ta là chủ của các ngươi, vậy sao các ngươi không kính trọng {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}}? {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} Vạn Quân phán. Hỡi các thầy tế lễ, các ngươi coi thường danh {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}}! \q Thế mà các ngươi hỏi: "Chúng tôi đã coi thường danh {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} ở chỗ nào?"

sw.L: Mwana humheshimu baba [yake], na mtumwa bwana wake. \q Basi ikiwa mimi [ni] baba, heshima {{deity_pronoun:yangu|Yangu}} [iko] wapi? Na ikiwa mimi [ni] bwana, kicho {{deity_pronoun:changu|Changu}} [kiko] wapi? asema {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} wa majeshi kwenu, enyi makuhani, mnaolidharau jina {{deity_pronoun:langu|Langu}}. \q Lakini mnasema, "Tumelidharau jina {{deity_pronoun:lako|Lako}} kwa namna gani?"
sw.B: Mwana humheshimu baba yake, na mtumishi humheshimu bwana wake. \q Ikiwa mimi ni baba, iko wapi heshima ninayostahili? Ikiwa mimi ni bwana, iko wapi hofu ninayostahili? asema {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} wa majeshi kwenu, enyi makuhani mnaolidharau jina {{deity_pronoun:langu|Langu}}. \q Lakini mnauliza, "Tumelidharau jina {{deity_pronoun:lako|Lako}} kwa njia gani?"
sw.R: Mwana humheshimu baba yake, na mtumishi humheshimu bwana wake. \q Mimi ni baba yenu, basi kwa nini hamniheshimu? Mimi ni bwana wenu, basi kwa nini hamnichi? anasema {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} wa majeshi. Enyi makuhani, mnalidharau jina {{deity_pronoun:langu|Langu}}! \q Lakini mnauliza, "Tumelidharau jina {{deity_pronoun:lako|Lako}} kwa namna gani?"

ko.L: 아들은 [자기] 아버지를 공경하고, 종은 자기 주인을 [공경한다]. \q 내가 아버지라면 나에 대한 공경이 어디 있느냐? 내가 주인이라면 나를 두려워함이 어디 있느냐? 내 이름을 멸시하는 제사장들아, 만군의 {{divine_name:주|야훼}}가 너희에게 말한다. \q 그런데 너희는 "저희가 어떻게 주님의 이름을 멸시하였습니까?" 하고 말한다.
ko.B: 아들은 아버지를 공경하고, 종은 주인을 공경한다. \q 내가 아버지라면, 나에게 마땅히 돌아올 공경은 어디 있느냐? 내가 주인이라면, 나에게 마땅히 돌아올 존경은 어디 있느냐? 내 이름을 멸시하는 제사장들아, 만군의 {{divine_name:주|야훼}}가 너희에게 말한다. \q 그런데 너희는 "저희가 무엇으로 주님의 이름을 멸시했습니까?" 하고 묻는다.
ko.R: 아들은 아버지를 공경하고, 종은 주인을 존경한다. \q 나는 너희의 아버지인데, 어째서 너희는 나를 공경하지 않느냐? 나는 너희의 주인인데, 어째서 너희는 나를 존경하지 않느냐? 하늘의 군대를 거느린 {{divine_name:주|야훼}}가 말한다. 제사장들아, 너희는 내 이름을 업신여기고 있다! \q 그런데 너희는 "저희가 어떻게 주님의 이름을 업신여겼다는 말입니까?" 하고 묻는다.

decisions.choice: a slave and his master: a servant owned by his master
decisions.reason: The word means a servant who belonged to his master, not a hired worker. Such a servant owed his master obedience and respect, as a son owed honor to his father. The LORD is both father (2:10; Isaiah 63:16) and master to his people. |

decisions.choice: where is my fear: where is the respect owed to me
decisions.reason: "Fear" here is reverence and respect, the honor a servant owes his master. |

decisions.choice: who despise my name: who treat the LORD himself with contempt
decisions.reason: The LORD's name stands for the LORD himself, as he has made himself known (Exodus 3:15). The priests, whose task was to honor it, show contempt for it by what they offer (verses 7-8). |

decisions.choice: the priests: the dispute of 1:6-2:9 is addressed to the priests
decisions.reason: The priests served at the altar of the rebuilt temple. The LORD's charge against them runs to 2:9, where it ends with his covenant with Levi. |

decisions.choice: slave (L), servant (B, R)
decisions.reason: The word follows the style guide's rule: "slave" at Literal, "servant" at Balanced and Readable, with the servant's position stated in m1. The people's question is set in double quotes and uses the deity_pronoun setting, because they speak to the LORD. |

decisions.choice: "esclave" (L), "serviteur" (B, R)
decisions.reason: As the style guide for ʿeved and the English.

decisions.choice: "vous, prêtres": God addresses the priests as "vous"
decisions.reason: As the term sheet for Malachi's disputations.

decisions.choice: "esclavo" (L); "siervo" (B, R)
decisions.reason: As in the English, L keeps the owned servant ("esclavo") and B and R say "siervo".

decisions.choice: "oh sacerdotes" (L); "sacerdotes" (B, R), with plural_you
decisions.reason: The priests are addressed in the plural through 1:6-2:9, so every "you" to them takes plural_you.

decisions.choice: "mtumwa" (L); "mtumishi" (B, R)
decisions.reason: As the Swahili style guide for doulos and the English "slave" / "servant".

decisions.choice: "종" at every level
decisions.reason: 'Eved is "종" at every level in these books (term sheet); the English has "slave" only at Literal.

decisions.choice: "đầy tớ" at every level for 'eved
decisions.reason: The term sheet keeps "đầy tớ" at every level, Literal included, and "nô lệ" only for slavery itself; here the point is a servant's respect for his master.

source.text: מַגִּישִׁ֤ים עַֽל־מִזְבְּחִי֙ לֶ֣חֶם מְגֹאָ֔ל וַאֲמַרְתֶּ֖ם בַּמֶּ֣ה גֵֽאַלְנ֑וּךָ בֶּאֱמָרְכֶ֕ם שֻׁלְחַ֥ן יְהוָ֖ה נִבְזֶ֥ה הֽוּא׃

records.literal_gloss: [You are] presenting on my altar defiled food. And you say, In what have we defiled you? In your saying, [The] table of Yahweh, it [is] despicable.

en.L: You are presenting defiled food on {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} altar. \q But you say, "How have we defiled {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}?" \q By your saying, \q "The table of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} is despicable."
en.B: You offer defiled food on {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} altar. \q Yet you ask, "In what way have we defiled {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}?" \q By saying, \q "The table of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} may be despised."
en.R: You put food on {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} altar that is not fit to offer. \q But you ask, "How have we made {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} unclean?" \q You do it by saying, "We do not need to respect {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}'s altar."

fr.L: Vous présentez sur {{deity_pronoun:mon|Mon}} autel une nourriture souillée. \q Mais vous dites : « En quoi {{deity_pronoun:t’|T’}}avons-nous souillé ? » \q En disant : \q « La table {{divine_name:du SEIGNEUR|de Yahvé}}, elle est méprisable. »
fr.B: Vous offrez sur {{deity_pronoun:mon|Mon}} autel une nourriture souillée. \q Et vous demandez : « En quoi {{deity_pronoun:t’|T’}}avons-nous souillé ? » \q En disant : \q « La table {{divine_name:du SEIGNEUR|de Yahvé}}, on peut la mépriser. »
fr.R: Vous mettez sur {{deity_pronoun:mon|Mon}} autel de la nourriture qui n’est pas digne d’être offerte. \q Mais vous dites : « Comment {{deity_pronoun:t’|T’}}avons-nous rendu impur ? » \q Vous le faites en disant : « L’autel {{divine_name:du SEIGNEUR|de Yahvé}} ne mérite pas de respect. »

es.L: {{plural_you:Ustedes presentan|Vosotros presentáis}} sobre {{deity_pronoun:mi|Mi}} altar pan inmundo. \q Pero {{plural_you:ustedes dicen|vosotros decís}}: «¿En qué {{deity_pronoun:te|Te}} hemos profanado?». \q En que {{plural_you:dicen|decís}}: \q «La mesa {{divine_name:del SEÑOR|de Yahvé}} es despreciable».
es.B: {{plural_you:Ofrecen|Ofrecéis}} sobre {{deity_pronoun:mi|Mi}} altar alimentos impuros. \q Pero {{plural_you:ustedes preguntan|vosotros preguntáis}}: «¿De qué manera {{deity_pronoun:te|Te}} hemos profanado?». \q Al decir: \q «La mesa {{divine_name:del SEÑOR|de Yahvé}} se puede despreciar».
es.R: {{plural_you:Ponen|Ponéis}} sobre {{deity_pronoun:mi|Mi}} altar alimentos que no sirven para ofrecer. \q Pero {{plural_you:ustedes preguntan|vosotros preguntáis}}: «¿Cómo {{deity_pronoun:te|Te}} hemos hecho impuro?». \q Lo {{plural_you:hacen|hacéis}} cuando {{plural_you:dicen|decís}}: «No hace falta respetar el altar {{divine_name:del SEÑOR|de Yahvé}}».

vi.L: Các ngươi dâng thức ăn ô uế trên bàn thờ {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}}. \q Nhưng các ngươi nói: "Chúng tôi đã làm ô uế {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} bằng cách nào?" \q Bằng việc các ngươi nói: \q "Bàn của {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} là đáng khinh."
vi.B: Các ngươi dâng thức ăn ô uế trên bàn thờ {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}}. \q Thế mà các ngươi hỏi: "Chúng tôi đã làm ô uế {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} ở chỗ nào?" \q Ấy là khi các ngươi nói: \q "Bàn của {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} có thể coi thường được."
vi.R: Các ngươi đặt trên bàn thờ {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} những thức ăn không xứng đáng để dâng. \q Thế mà các ngươi hỏi: "Chúng tôi đã làm ô uế {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} ở chỗ nào?" \q Ấy là khi các ngươi nói: "Chúng ta chẳng cần tôn trọng bàn thờ của {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}}."

sw.L: Mnaleta chakula kilicho najisi juu ya madhabahu {{deity_pronoun:yangu|Yangu}}. \q Lakini mnasema, "Tumekutia unajisi kwa namna gani?" \q Kwa kusema kwenu, \q "Meza ya {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} inadharaulika."
sw.B: Mnatoa chakula kilicho najisi juu ya madhabahu {{deity_pronoun:yangu|Yangu}}. \q Lakini mnauliza, "Tumekutia unajisi kwa njia gani?" \q Kwa kusema, \q "Meza ya {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} inaweza kudharauliwa."
sw.R: Mnaweka juu ya madhabahu {{deity_pronoun:yangu|Yangu}} chakula kisichofaa kutolewa. \q Lakini mnauliza, "Tumekufanya najisi kwa namna gani?" \q Mnafanya hivyo kwa kusema, "Hatuhitaji kuiheshimu madhabahu ya {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}."

ko.L: 너희가 내 제단 위에 더러운 음식을 바치고 있다. \q 그런데 너희는 "저희가 어떻게 주님을 더럽혔습니까?" 하고 말한다. \q 그것은 너희가 \q "{{divine_name:주|야훼}}의 상은 하찮다" 하고 말하는 것으로써이다.
ko.B: 너희는 내 제단에 더러운 음식을 바친다. \q 그런데 너희는 "저희가 무엇으로 주님을 더럽혔습니까?" 하고 묻는다. \q 너희가 내 제단을 두고 \q "{{divine_name:주|야훼}}의 상은 업신여겨도 된다" 하고 말하기 때문이다.
ko.R: 너희는 바칠 수 없는 음식을 내 제단에 올려놓는다. \q 그런데 너희는 "저희가 어떻게 주님을 더럽혔다는 말입니까?" 하고 묻는다. \q 너희가 "{{divine_name:주|야훼}}의 제단은 존중하지 않아도 된다" 하고 말하기 때문이다.

decisions.choice: defiled food: offerings unfit for the altar
decisions.reason: The sacrifices are called the "food" of God (Leviticus 21:6, 8; 3:11), not because he needs to eat but because they are presented at his table. Verse 8 says what makes them defiled. |

decisions.choice: the table of the LORD: the altar
decisions.reason: Ezekiel 41:22 and 44:16 call the altar "the table that is before the LORD". The priests treat the place where the LORD is served as of no account. |

decisions.choice: How have we defiled you?: defiling the offering defiles the LORD
decisions.reason: The Hebrew says "defiled you": to treat his altar with contempt is to treat the LORD himself so. The Greek translation is generally said to read "defiled it", referring to the food.

decisions.choice: the people's words in double quotes
decisions.reason: The priests did not say these words aloud; their actions say them. They are set as quoted words, as the book quotes the people throughout. Readable says "altar" for "table", the sense of m2. |

decisions.choice: "la mesa del SEÑOR" (L, B); "el altar del SEÑOR" (R)
decisions.reason: The table of the LORD is his altar; L and B keep the image, R names the altar, as the English R does.

source.text: וְכִֽי־תַגִּשׁ֨וּן עִוֵּ֤ר לִזְבֹּ֨חַ֙ אֵ֣ין רָ֔ע וְכִ֥י תַגִּ֛ישׁוּ פִּסֵּ֥חַ וְחֹלֶ֖ה אֵ֣ין רָ֑ע הַקְרִיבֵ֨הוּ נָ֜א לְפֶחָתֶ֗ךָ הֲיִּרְצְךָ֙א֚וֹ הֲיִשָּׂ֣א פָנֶ֔יךָ אָמַ֖ר יְהוָ֥ה צְבָאֽוֹת׃

records.literal_gloss: And when you present a blind [one] for sacrifice, [is it] not evil? And when you present [the] lame and [the] sick, [is it] not evil? Present it, please, to your governor; will he be pleased with you or lift up your face? says Yahweh of hosts.

en.L: And when you present a blind [animal] for sacrifice, is it not evil? \q And when you present the lame and the sick, is it not evil? \q Present it, please, to your governor; will he be pleased with you or lift up your face? \q says {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} of hosts.
en.B: When you offer blind animals in sacrifice, is that not wrong? \q When you offer animals that are lame or sick, is that not wrong? \q Just try offering such a thing to your governor! Would he be pleased with you or receive you kindly? \q says {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} of Armies.
en.R: You bring blind animals to sacrifice. Is that not wrong? \q You bring animals that are lame or sick. Is that not wrong? \q Try giving them to your governor! Would he be pleased with you? Would he accept you? says {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} of Armies.

fr.L: Et quand vous présentez [une bête] aveugle pour le sacrifice, n’est-ce pas mal ? \q Et quand vous présentez la boiteuse et la malade, n’est-ce pas mal ? \q Présente-la donc à ton gouverneur ; t’accueillera-t-il avec faveur, ou relèvera-t-il ta face ? \q dit {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} des armées.
fr.B: Quand vous offrez en sacrifice des bêtes aveugles, n’est-ce pas mal ? \q Quand vous offrez des bêtes boiteuses ou malades, n’est-ce pas mal ? \q Essaie donc de l’offrir à ton gouverneur ! Sera-t-il content de toi, ou te fera-t-il bon accueil ? \q dit {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} des armées.
fr.R: Vous apportez des animaux aveugles pour les sacrifier. N’est-ce pas mal ? \q Vous apportez des animaux boiteux ou malades. N’est-ce pas mal ? \q Essaie de les donner à ton gouverneur ! Serait-il content de toi ? T’accueillerait-il bien ? dit {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} des armées.

es.L: Y cuando {{plural_you:presentan|presentáis}} [un animal] ciego para sacrificar, ¿no es malo? \q Y cuando {{plural_you:presentan|presentáis}} el cojo y el enfermo, ¿no es malo? \q {{plural_you:Preséntenlo|Presentadlo}}, pues, a {{plural_you:su gobernador|vuestro gobernador}}; ¿se agradará de {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}} o {{plural_you:les|os}} alzará el rostro? \q dice {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} de los ejércitos.
es.B: Cuando {{plural_you:ofrecen|ofrecéis}} animales ciegos en sacrificio, ¿no está mal? \q Cuando {{plural_you:ofrecen|ofrecéis}} animales cojos o enfermos, ¿no está mal? \q ¡{{plural_you:Intenten|Intentad}} ofrecerle algo así a {{plural_you:su gobernador|vuestro gobernador}}! ¿Se agradaría de {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}} o {{plural_you:los|os}} recibiría con favor? \q dice {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} de los Ejércitos.
es.R: {{plural_you:Traen|Traéis}} animales ciegos para sacrificarlos. ¿No está mal eso? \q {{plural_you:Traen|Traéis}} animales cojos o enfermos. ¿No está mal eso? \q ¡{{plural_you:Intenten|Intentad}} dárselos a {{plural_you:su gobernador|vuestro gobernador}}! ¿Se agradaría de {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}}? ¿{{plural_you:Los|Os}} aceptaría?, dice {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} de los Ejércitos.

vi.L: Khi các ngươi dâng [con vật] mù làm sinh tế, chẳng phải là điều ác sao? \q Khi các ngươi dâng con què và con bệnh, chẳng phải là điều ác sao? \q Hãy thử dâng nó cho quan tổng đốc của các ngươi xem; ông ấy có hài lòng về các ngươi hay nâng mặt các ngươi lên không? \q {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} Vạn Quân phán.
vi.B: Khi các ngươi dâng những con vật mù làm sinh tế, chẳng phải là sai trái sao? \q Khi các ngươi dâng những con vật què hay bệnh, chẳng phải là sai trái sao? \q Thử đem dâng những thứ ấy cho quan tổng đốc của các ngươi xem! Ông ấy có hài lòng về các ngươi hay tiếp đón các ngươi tử tế không? \q {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} Vạn Quân phán.
vi.R: Các ngươi đem những con vật mù đến dâng làm sinh tế. Như vậy chẳng phải là sai trái sao? \q Các ngươi đem những con vật què hay bệnh đến. Như vậy chẳng phải là sai trái sao? \q Thử đem chúng biếu quan tổng đốc của các ngươi xem! Ông ấy có hài lòng về các ngươi không? Ông ấy có chấp nhận các ngươi không? {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} Vạn Quân phán.

sw.L: Na mnapoleta [mnyama] kipofu kwa ajili ya dhabihu, je, si uovu? \q Na mnapoleta aliye kilema na aliye mgonjwa, je, si uovu? \q Mpelekee liwali wako tafadhali; je, atapendezwa nawe au kukuinulia uso? \q asema {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} wa majeshi.
sw.B: Mnapotoa wanyama vipofu kuwa dhabihu, je, si vibaya? \q Mnapotoa wanyama vilema au wagonjwa, je, si vibaya? \q Jaribu kumpelekea liwali wako kitu kama hicho! Je, angependezwa nawe au kukupokea kwa wema? \q asema {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} wa majeshi.
sw.R: Mnaleta wanyama vipofu kuwa dhabihu. Je, si vibaya? \q Mnaleta wanyama vilema au wagonjwa. Je, si vibaya? \q Jaribuni kumpa liwali wenu wanyama hao! Je, angefurahishwa nanyi? Angewakubali? anasema {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} wa majeshi.

ko.L: 너희가 눈먼 [짐승을] 제물로 바칠 때, 그것이 악하지 않으냐? \q 너희가 다리 저는 것과 병든 것을 바칠 때, 그것이 악하지 않으냐? \q 그것을 너희 총독에게 바쳐 보아라. 그가 너희를 기뻐하겠느냐? 너희 얼굴을 들어 주겠느냐? \q 만군의 {{divine_name:주|야훼}}가 말한다.
ko.B: 너희가 눈먼 짐승을 제물로 바치는 것이 잘못이 아니냐? \q 다리 저는 짐승과 병든 짐승을 바치는 것이 잘못이 아니냐? \q 그런 것을 너희 총독에게 바쳐 보아라! 그가 너희를 반기겠느냐? 너희를 너그럽게 맞아 주겠느냐? \q 만군의 {{divine_name:주|야훼}}가 말한다.
ko.R: 너희는 눈먼 짐승을 제물로 가져온다. 그것이 잘못이 아니냐? \q 너희는 다리 저는 짐승이나 병든 짐승을 가져온다. 그것이 잘못이 아니냐? \q 그런 것을 너희 총독에게 바쳐 보아라! 그가 너희를 기뻐하겠느냐? 너희를 반가이 맞아 주겠느냐? 하늘의 군대를 거느린 {{divine_name:주|야훼}}가 말한다.

decisions.choice: blind, lame and sick animals: animals the law forbade for sacrifice
decisions.reason: Animals for sacrifice had to be without defect: blind, lame or sick animals were not to be offered (Leviticus 22:20-25; Deuteronomy 15:21). The priests were letting people offer what they did not want themselves. |

decisions.choice: your governor: the Persian governor of Judah
decisions.reason: Judah was a province of the Persian empire, ruled by a governor, as Zerubbabel had been (Haggai 1:1) and Nehemiah later was (Nehemiah 5:14-15). People brought gifts to a governor, and no one would dare give him a sick animal. |

decisions.choice: lift up your face: receive you with favor
decisions.reason: To lift someone's face is to accept him, to grant his request (Genesis 32:21; Job 42:8). The same idiom returns in verse 9. |

decisions.choice: is it not evil?: a question
decisions.reason: The words can be read as the LORD's question or as the priests' careless claim ("It does not matter!"). Read either way, the LORD's verdict is plain.

decisions.choice: animals (B, R); wrong (B, R)
decisions.reason: Literal brackets "[animal]"; Balanced and Readable say "animals". Balanced and Readable say "wrong" for "evil", which here means a wrong done. |

decisions.choice: "présente-la ... ton gouverneur ... toi", singular
decisions.reason: The Hebrew turns to the singular here, addressing each priest; French switches number with it, as the term sheet asks.

decisions.choice: "alzará el rostro"
decisions.reason: L keeps the idiom "lift up the face" (receive with favor); B and R give its sense.

decisions.choice: "liwali wako", singular "you" (L, B)
decisions.reason: The Hebrew turns to the singular here ("your governor", "with you"); Literal and Balanced keep it, Readable uses the plural as the English does. "Liwali" is the term sheet's word for a governor.

decisions.choice: "quan tổng đốc" for pechah
decisions.reason: The term sheet's word for the Persian governor (pechah), as Ezra and Haggai.

source.text: וְעַתָּ֛ה חַלּוּ־נָ֥א פְנֵי־אֵ֖ל וִֽיחָנֵ֑נוּמִיֶּדְכֶם֙ הָ֣יְתָה זֹּ֔את הֲיִשָּׂ֤א מִכֶּם֙ פָּנִ֔ים אָמַ֖ר יְהוָ֥ה צְבָאֽוֹת׃

records.literal_gloss: And now, entreat, please, [the] face of God, that he may be gracious to us. From your hand this has been; will he lift up faces from you? says Yahweh of hosts.

en.L: And now, entreat the face of God, that {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} may be gracious to us! \q From your hand this has come; \q will {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} lift up the face of any of you? says {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} of hosts.
en.B: So now, plead with God to be gracious to us! \q With such offerings from your hands, \q will {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} show favor to any of you? says {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} of Armies.
en.R: So now, go ahead and ask God to be kind to us! \q But when you bring offerings like these, \q will {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} accept any of you? says {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} of Armies.

fr.L: Et maintenant, apaisez donc la face de Dieu, pour qu’{{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} nous fasse grâce ! \q C’est de votre main que cela est venu ; \q relèvera-t-{{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} la face de l’un de vous ? dit {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} des armées.
fr.B: Alors maintenant, implorez donc Dieu pour qu’{{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} nous fasse grâce ! \q Avec de telles offrandes de vos mains, \q accordera-t-{{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} {{deity_pronoun:sa|Sa}} faveur à l’un de vous ? dit {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} des armées.
fr.R: Allez-y, demandez à Dieu d’être bon envers nous ! \q Mais quand vous apportez de telles offrandes, \q acceptera-t-{{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} l’un de vous ? dit {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} des armées.

es.L: Y ahora, {{plural_you:imploren|implorad}} el favor de Dios, para que {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}} tenga piedad de nosotros. \q De {{plural_you:sus manos|vuestras manos}} ha venido esto; \q ¿alzará {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}} el rostro de alguno de {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}}?, dice {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} de los ejércitos.
es.B: Así que ahora, {{plural_you:supliquen|suplicad}} a Dios que tenga piedad de nosotros. \q Con tales ofrendas en {{plural_you:sus manos|vuestras manos}}, \q ¿mostrará {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}} favor a alguno de {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}}?, dice {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} de los Ejércitos.
es.R: Así que ahora, ¡{{plural_you:vayan|id}} y {{plural_you:pídanle|pedidle}} a Dios que sea bondadoso con nosotros! \q Pero cuando {{plural_you:traen|traéis}} ofrendas como estas, \q ¿aceptará {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}} a alguno de {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}}?, dice {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} de los Ejércitos.

vi.L: Vậy bây giờ, hãy cầu xin ơn của Đức Chúa Trời, để {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} thương xót chúng ta! \q Điều này đến từ tay các ngươi; \q {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} có nâng mặt ai trong các ngươi lên chăng? {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} Vạn Quân phán.
vi.B: Vậy bây giờ, hãy nài xin Đức Chúa Trời ban ơn cho chúng ta đi! \q Với những lễ vật như thế từ tay các ngươi, \q {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} có đoái thương ai trong các ngươi không? {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} Vạn Quân phán.
vi.R: Vậy bây giờ, cứ thử cầu xin Đức Chúa Trời thương xót chúng ta xem! \q Nhưng khi các ngươi đem đến những lễ vật như thế, \q {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} có chấp nhận ai trong các ngươi không? {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} Vạn Quân phán.

sw.L: Basi sasa, utafuteni uso wa Mungu, ili atufanyie neema! \q Hili limetoka mkononi mwenu; \q je, atamwinulia uso yeyote kati yenu? asema {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} wa majeshi.
sw.B: Basi sasa, mwombeni Mungu atufanyie neema! \q Mkileta matoleo kama haya mikononi mwenu, \q je, atamwonea fadhili yeyote kati yenu? asema {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} wa majeshi.
sw.R: Basi sasa, haya, mwombeni Mungu atuhurumie! \q Lakini mnapoleta matoleo kama haya, \q je, atamkubali yeyote kati yenu? anasema {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} wa majeshi.

ko.L: 이제 하나님의 얼굴을 구하여 그분께서 우리에게 은혜를 베푸시게 하여라! \q 너희 손에서 이런 것이 나왔으니, \q 그분께서 너희 가운데 누구의 얼굴인들 들어 주시겠느냐? 만군의 {{divine_name:주|야훼}}가 말한다.
ko.B: 이제 하나님께 우리에게 은혜를 베풀어 달라고 간청해 보아라! \q 너희 손으로 이런 제물을 바치면서, \q 그분께서 너희 가운데 누구를 너그럽게 대하시겠느냐? 만군의 {{divine_name:주|야훼}}가 말한다.
ko.R: 자, 이제 하나님께 우리에게 친절을 베풀어 달라고 빌어 보아라! \q 그러나 너희가 이런 제물을 가져오면서, \q 그분께서 너희 가운데 누구를 받아 주시겠느냐? 하늘의 군대를 거느린 {{divine_name:주|야훼}}가 말한다.

decisions.choice: entreat the favor of God: seek his goodwill in prayer
decisions.reason: The phrase means "soften the face" of someone, that is, to seek favor (Exodus 32:11; 1 Kings 13:6). |

decisions.choice: a call to prayer, spoken in irony
decisions.reason: The prophet urges the priests to pray for the people ("us"), but with offerings like theirs the LORD will not hear. The question at the end expects the answer "no". |

decisions.choice: from your hand this has come: this is your doing
decisions.reason: The defective offerings came from the priests' own hands, so the LORD's refusal is their own fault. |

decisions.choice: entreat the favor (L), plead with God (B), ask God to be kind (R)
decisions.reason: Literal keeps the picture of the face (m1). Balanced and Readable add "with such offerings" and "offerings like these" to make "this" plain. |

decisions.choice: "apaisez donc" (L), "implorez donc" (B), "Allez-y, demandez" (R)
decisions.reason: French "donc" and "Allez-y" carry the irony the meaning decision notes.

decisions.choice: "imploren el favor de Dios" (L); "supliquen a Dios" (B); "pídanle a Dios que sea bondadoso" (R)
decisions.reason: The idiom is worded as in Zechariah 7:2 and 8:21 at L and R; the call is ironic, as the meaning decision says.

decisions.choice: "하나님" and "그분께서 … 베푸시게" with -시-
decisions.reason: God speaks of himself as "God" in the third person, voicing the priests' prayer in irony (meaning decision), and the English marks it with deity spans; Korean gives the honorific here because the words imitate the people's own prayer.

source.text: מִ֤י גַם־בָּכֶם֙ וְיִסְגֹּ֣ר דְּלָתַ֔יִם וְלֹֽא־תָאִ֥ירוּ מִזְבְּחִ֖י חִנָּ֑ם אֵֽין־לִ֨י חֵ֜פֶץ בָּכֶ֗ם אָמַר֙ יְהוָ֣ה צְבָא֔וֹת וּמִנְחָ֖ה לֹֽא־אֶרְצֶ֥ה מִיֶּדְכֶֽם׃

records.literal_gloss: Who also among you [is there] that he would shut the doors, and you would not kindle my altar in vain? I have no pleasure in you, says Yahweh of hosts, and an offering I will not accept from your hand.

en.L: Who is there even among you who would shut the doors, \q so that you would not kindle {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} altar in vain? \q I have no pleasure in you, says {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} of hosts, \q and an offering I will not accept from your hand.
en.B: If only one of you would close the temple doors \q and stop you from lighting useless fires on {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} altar! \q I have no pleasure in you, says {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} of Armies, \q and I will not accept an offering from your hands.
en.R: I wish someone among you would lock the temple doors, \q so that you would stop lighting useless fires on {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} altar! \q I am not pleased with you, says {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} of Armies. \q I will not accept any offering you bring.

fr.L: Qui donc, parmi vous, fermerait les portes, \q pour que vous n’allumiez pas {{deity_pronoun:mon|Mon}} autel pour rien ? \q Je ne prends pas de plaisir en vous, dit {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} des armées, \q et une offrande, je ne l’accepterai pas de votre main.
fr.B: Si seulement l’un de vous fermait les portes du temple, \q pour que vous cessiez d’allumer des feux inutiles sur {{deity_pronoun:mon|Mon}} autel ! \q Je ne prends aucun plaisir en vous, dit {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} des armées, \q et je n’accepterai pas d’offrande de vos mains.
fr.R: J’aimerais que quelqu’un parmi vous ferme à clé les portes du temple, \q pour que vous arrêtiez d’allumer des feux inutiles sur {{deity_pronoun:mon|Mon}} autel ! \q Je ne suis pas content de vous, dit {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} des armées. \q Je n’accepterai aucune offrande que vous m’apporterez.

es.L: ¿Quién hay también entre {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}} que cierre las puertas, \q para que no {{plural_you:enciendan|encendáis}} en vano {{deity_pronoun:mi|Mi}} altar? \q No tengo complacencia en {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}}, dice {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} de los ejércitos, \q y no aceptaré ofrenda de {{plural_you:su mano|vuestra mano}}.
es.B: ¡Ojalá alguno de {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}} cerrara las puertas del templo \q para que no {{plural_you:encendieran|encendierais}} fuegos inútiles en {{deity_pronoun:mi|Mi}} altar! \q No me agradan {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}}, dice {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} de los Ejércitos, \q y no aceptaré ofrenda de {{plural_you:sus manos|vuestras manos}}.
es.R: ¡Ojalá alguno de {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}} cerrara con llave las puertas del templo, \q para que {{plural_you:dejaran|dejarais}} de encender fuegos inútiles en {{deity_pronoun:mi|Mi}} altar! \q No estoy contento con {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}}, dice {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} de los Ejércitos. \q No aceptaré ninguna ofrenda que me {{plural_you:traigan|traigáis}}.

vi.L: Ước gì trong các ngươi có người đóng các cửa lại, \q để các ngươi khỏi nhóm lửa trên bàn thờ {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} cách vô ích! \q Ta chẳng vui lòng về các ngươi, {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} Vạn Quân phán, \q và {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} sẽ không nhận lễ vật từ tay các ngươi.
vi.B: Ước gì có một người trong các ngươi đóng cửa đền thờ lại, \q để các ngươi thôi nhóm lửa vô ích trên bàn thờ {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}}! \q Ta chẳng vui lòng về các ngươi, {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} Vạn Quân phán, \q và {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} sẽ không nhận lễ vật nào từ tay các ngươi.
vi.R: Ước gì có ai trong các ngươi khóa cửa đền thờ lại, \q để các ngươi thôi đốt lửa vô ích trên bàn thờ {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}}! \q Ta không hài lòng về các ngươi, {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} Vạn Quân phán. \q Ta sẽ không nhận bất cứ lễ vật nào các ngươi đem đến.

sw.L: Ni nani hata kati yenu atakayefunga milango, \q ili msiwashe moto bure juu ya madhabahu {{deity_pronoun:yangu|Yangu}}? \q Sina furaha nanyi, asema {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} wa majeshi, \q wala sitapokea sadaka kutoka mkononi mwenu.
sw.B: Laiti mmoja wenu angefunga milango ya hekalu \q ili msiwashe moto usiofaa kitu juu ya madhabahu {{deity_pronoun:yangu|Yangu}}! \q Sipendezwi nanyi, asema {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} wa majeshi, \q wala sitapokea sadaka kutoka mikononi mwenu.
sw.R: Laiti mtu mmoja kati yenu angefunga milango ya hekalu, \q ili mwache kuwasha moto usiofaa kitu juu ya madhabahu {{deity_pronoun:yangu|Yangu}}! \q Sifurahishwi nanyi, anasema {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} wa majeshi. \q Sitapokea sadaka yoyote mnayoleta.

ko.L: 너희 가운데 누가 성전 문들을 닫아서, \q 너희가 내 제단에 헛되이 불을 피우지 않게 하겠느냐? \q 나는 너희를 기뻐하지 않는다. 만군의 {{divine_name:주|야훼}}가 말한다. \q 내가 너희 손에서 예물을 받지 않겠다.
ko.B: 너희 가운데 누군가가 성전 문을 닫아 걸어서, \q 너희가 내 제단에 쓸데없이 불을 피우지 못하게 하면 좋겠다! \q 나는 너희가 기쁘지 않다. 만군의 {{divine_name:주|야훼}}가 말한다. \q 나는 너희 손에서 예물을 받지 않겠다.
ko.R: 너희 가운데 누가 성전 문을 잠가 버리면 좋겠다. \q 그러면 너희가 내 제단에 쓸데없이 불을 피우지 않을 것이다! \q 나는 너희가 마음에 들지 않는다. 하늘의 군대를 거느린 {{divine_name:주|야훼}}가 말한다. \q 너희가 가져오는 예물은 무엇이든 받지 않겠다.

decisions.choice: who among you would shut the doors?: a wish
decisions.reason: A question beginning "who" can express a wish (2 Samuel 15:4; Psalm 55:7). The LORD would rather have the temple closed than receive such worship. |

decisions.choice: the doors: the gates of the temple courts
decisions.reason: The doors are those of the temple and its courts, where the altar stood. Shutting them would end the sacrifices. |

decisions.choice: offering: a gift brought to God
decisions.reason: The word is used for the grain offering (Leviticus 2:1) and for offerings in general. Here it means any gift the priests bring. |

decisions.choice: the temple doors (B, R)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say which doors are meant (m2). |

decisions.choice: "ofrenda"
decisions.reason: Minhah is "ofrenda" at every level, the general word for a gift brought to God.

decisions.choice: the Hebrew question "Who among you would shut the doors?" is a wish: "Ước gì ..." at every level
decisions.reason: A Vietnamese question here would read as a real question; the meaning decision says it is a wish.

source.text: כִּ֣י מִמִּזְרַח־שֶׁ֜מֶשׁ וְעַד־מְבוֹא֗וֹ גָּד֤וֹל שְׁמִי֙ בַּגּוֹיִ֔ם וּבְכָל־מָק֗וֹם מֻקְטָ֥ר מֻגָּ֛שׁ לִשְׁמִ֖י וּמִנְחָ֣ה טְהוֹרָ֑ה כִּֽי־גָד֤וֹל שְׁמִי֙ בַּגּוֹיִ֔ם אָמַ֖ר יְהוָ֥ה צְבָאֽוֹת׃

records.literal_gloss: For from [the] rising of [the] sun and to its setting great [is] my name among the nations, and in every place incense is offered to my name, and a pure offering; for great [is] my name among the nations, says Yahweh of hosts.

en.L: For from the rising of the sun to its setting great [is] {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} name among the nations, \q and in every place incense is brought near to {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} name, and a pure offering; \q for great [is] {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} name among the nations, \q says {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} of hosts.
en.B: From where the sun rises to where it sets, {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} name is great among the nations. \q In every place incense is offered to {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} name, and pure offerings, \q because {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} name is great among the nations, \q says {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} of Armies.
en.R: From where the sun rises to where it sets, {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} name is honored among the nations. \q Everywhere people burn incense to {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} and bring offerings that are pure. \q My name is great among the nations, \q says {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} of Armies.

fr.L: Car du lever du soleil jusqu’à son coucher, grand [est] {{deity_pronoun:mon|Mon}} nom parmi les nations, \q et en tout lieu on fait monter l’encens pour {{deity_pronoun:mon|Mon}} nom, et une offrande pure ; \q car grand [est] {{deity_pronoun:mon|Mon}} nom parmi les nations, \q dit {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} des armées.
fr.B: Du lieu où le soleil se lève jusqu’à celui où il se couche, {{deity_pronoun:mon|Mon}} nom est grand parmi les nations. \q En tout lieu on offre de l’encens à {{deity_pronoun:mon|Mon}} nom, et des offrandes pures, \q car {{deity_pronoun:mon|Mon}} nom est grand parmi les nations, \q dit {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} des armées.
fr.R: De l’endroit où le soleil se lève jusqu’à celui où il se couche, {{deity_pronoun:mon|Mon}} nom est honoré parmi les nations. \q Partout, des gens brûlent de l’encens pour {{deity_pronoun:moi|Moi}} et apportent des offrandes pures. \q Mon nom est grand parmi les nations, \q dit {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} des armées.

es.L: Porque desde la salida del sol hasta su ocaso, grande [es] {{deity_pronoun:mi|Mi}} nombre entre las naciones, \q y en todo lugar se ofrece incienso a {{deity_pronoun:mi|Mi}} nombre, y ofrenda pura; \q porque grande [es] {{deity_pronoun:mi|Mi}} nombre entre las naciones, \q dice {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} de los ejércitos.
es.B: Desde donde sale el sol hasta donde se pone, {{deity_pronoun:mi|Mi}} nombre es grande entre las naciones. \q En todo lugar se ofrece incienso a {{deity_pronoun:mi|Mi}} nombre, y ofrendas puras, \q porque {{deity_pronoun:mi|Mi}} nombre es grande entre las naciones, \q dice {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} de los Ejércitos.
es.R: Desde donde sale el sol hasta donde se pone, {{deity_pronoun:mi|Mi}} nombre es honrado entre las naciones. \q En todas partes la gente {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} quema incienso y {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} trae ofrendas puras. \q Mi nombre es grande entre las naciones, \q dice {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} de los Ejércitos.

vi.L: Vì từ nơi mặt trời mọc đến nơi mặt trời lặn, danh {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} [là] lớn giữa các dân tộc, \q và ở mọi nơi, người ta dâng hương cho danh {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}}, cùng lễ vật thanh sạch; \q vì danh {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} [là] lớn giữa các dân tộc, \q {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} Vạn Quân phán.
vi.B: Từ nơi mặt trời mọc đến nơi mặt trời lặn, danh {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} được tôn cao giữa các dân tộc. \q Ở khắp mọi nơi, người ta dâng hương và lễ vật thanh sạch cho danh {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}}, \q vì danh {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} được tôn cao giữa các dân tộc, \q {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} Vạn Quân phán.
vi.R: Từ phương đông đến phương tây, danh {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} được tôn kính giữa các dân tộc. \q Khắp nơi người ta đốt hương dâng cho {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} và đem đến những lễ vật thanh sạch. \q Danh {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} được tôn cao giữa các dân tộc, \q {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} Vạn Quân phán.

sw.L: Kwa maana tangu kuchomoza kwa jua hata kutua kwake jina {{deity_pronoun:langu|Langu}} [ni] kuu kati ya mataifa, \q na kila mahali uvumba unatolewa kwa jina {{deity_pronoun:langu|Langu}}, na sadaka safi; \q kwa maana jina {{deity_pronoun:langu|Langu}} [ni] kuu kati ya mataifa, \q asema {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} wa majeshi.
sw.B: Tangu jua linapochomoza hadi linapotua, jina {{deity_pronoun:langu|Langu}} ni kuu kati ya mataifa. \q Kila mahali uvumba unatolewa kwa jina {{deity_pronoun:langu|Langu}}, pamoja na sadaka safi, \q kwa sababu jina {{deity_pronoun:langu|Langu}} ni kuu kati ya mataifa, \q asema {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} wa majeshi.
sw.R: Tangu jua linapochomoza hadi linapotua, jina {{deity_pronoun:langu|Langu}} linaheshimiwa kati ya mataifa. \q Kila mahali watu wanafukiza uvumba kwa ajili {{deity_pronoun:yangu|Yangu}} na kuleta sadaka safi. \q Jina langu ni kuu kati ya mataifa, \q anasema {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} wa majeshi.

ko.L: 해 뜨는 곳에서부터 해 지는 곳까지 내 이름이 민족들 가운데서 크고, \q 곳곳에서 내 이름에 분향하며 깨끗한 예물을 바친다. \q 내 이름이 민족들 가운데서 크기 때문이다. \q 만군의 {{divine_name:주|야훼}}가 말한다.
ko.B: 해 뜨는 곳에서 해 지는 곳까지, 민족들 가운데서 내 이름이 크다. \q 곳곳에서 사람들이 내 이름에 향을 피우고 깨끗한 예물을 바친다. \q 민족들 가운데서 내 이름이 크기 때문이다. \q 만군의 {{divine_name:주|야훼}}가 말한다.
ko.R: 해 뜨는 곳에서 해 지는 곳까지, 여러 민족이 내 이름을 높인다. \q 어디에서나 사람들이 나에게 향을 피우고 깨끗한 예물을 바친다. \q 내 이름은 민족들 가운데서 크다. \q 하늘의 군대를 거느린 {{divine_name:주|야훼}}가 말한다.

decisions.choice: from the rising of the sun to its setting: from east to west, all over the world
decisions.reason: The phrase means the whole earth (Psalm 50:1; 113:3; Isaiah 45:6). |

decisions.choice: my name is great among the nations: the LORD honored by the nations, now or in time to come
alternatives: my name will be great among the nations
decisions.reason: The Hebrew has no verb "is" or "will be", and the offering is described with participles, so the verse may speak of the present or of the future. Read as present, it may mean that the nations, in their own way, honor the God of heaven, or that Jews scattered among the nations worship him; read as future, it is a promise like Zephaniah 2:11 and Isaiah 45:6. Either way it shames the priests of verse 10. From early times Christian writers read it of the church's worship among the nations. The text leaves the time open, and the wording here keeps the Hebrew present.

decisions.choice: incense is offered: offerings burned, as the smoke of incense
decisions.reason: The first word means something made to go up in smoke, usually incense. The offerings brought "in every place" contrast with the defiled offerings in the one temple. |

decisions.choice: is honored (R); burn incense to me (R)
decisions.reason: Readable says "honored" for "great" in the first line and keeps "great" in the third, and says "burn incense to me" for "incense is offered to my name", since the name stands for the LORD himself. |

decisions.choice: "Jina langu" at the start of a line (R), written plainly
decisions.reason: The English Readable writes "My name" at the start of a sentence without a span; Swahili follows it (Swahili style guide 7: a pronoun at the start of a sentence is written plainly with its capital).

source.text: וְאַתֶּ֖ם מְחַלְּלִ֣ים אוֹת֑וֹ בֶּאֱמָרְכֶ֗ם שֻׁלְחַ֤ן אֲדֹנָי֙ מְגֹאָ֣ל ה֔וּא וְנִיב֖וֹ נִבְזֶ֥ה אָכְלֽוֹ׃

records.literal_gloss: But you [are] profaning it in your saying, [The] table of [the] Lord, it [is] defiled, and its fruit, its food, [is] despicable.

en.L: But you are profaning it \q in your saying, "The table of the Lord, it is defiled, \q and its fruit, its food, is despicable."
en.B: But you profane it \q by saying, "The Lord's table is defiled, \q and the food on it can be despised."
en.R: But you treat {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} name as if it were not holy. \q You say, "The Lord's altar is unclean, \q and the food offered on it does not deserve respect."

fr.L: Mais vous, vous le profanez \q en disant : « La table du Seigneur, elle est souillée, \q et son fruit, sa nourriture, est méprisable. »
fr.B: Mais vous, vous le profanez \q en disant : « La table du Seigneur est souillée, \q et la nourriture qu’on y met peut être méprisée. »
fr.R: Mais vous traitez {{deity_pronoun:mon|Mon}} nom comme s’il n’était pas saint. \q Vous dites : « L’autel du Seigneur est impur, \q et la nourriture qu’on y offre ne mérite pas de respect. »

es.L: Pero {{plural_you:ustedes lo profanan|vosotros lo profanáis}} \q cuando {{plural_you:dicen|decís}}: «La mesa del Señor es inmunda, \q y su fruto, su alimento, es despreciable».
es.B: Pero {{plural_you:ustedes lo profanan|vosotros lo profanáis}} \q al decir: «La mesa del Señor está contaminada, \q y la comida que hay sobre ella se puede despreciar».
es.R: Pero {{plural_you:ustedes tratan|vosotros tratáis}} {{deity_pronoun:mi|Mi}} nombre como si no fuera santo. \q {{plural_you:Dicen|Decís}}: «El altar del Señor es impuro, \q y la comida que se ofrece en él no merece respeto».

vi.L: Nhưng các ngươi xúc phạm danh ấy \q khi các ngươi nói: "Bàn của Chúa, nó bị ô uế, \q và hoa lợi của nó, thức ăn của nó, là đáng khinh."
vi.B: Nhưng các ngươi xúc phạm danh ấy \q khi nói: "Bàn của Chúa đã bị ô uế, \q và thức ăn trên đó có thể coi thường được."
vi.R: Nhưng các ngươi đối xử với danh {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} như thể danh ấy không thánh. \q Các ngươi nói: "Bàn thờ của Chúa là ô uế, \q và thức ăn dâng trên đó chẳng đáng tôn trọng."

sw.L: Lakini ninyi mnalitia unajisi \q kwa kusema kwenu, "Meza ya Bwana, imetiwa unajisi, \q na tunda lake, chakula chake, kinadharaulika."
sw.B: Lakini ninyi mnalitia unajisi \q kwa kusema, "Meza ya Bwana imetiwa unajisi, \q na chakula kilicho juu yake kinaweza kudharauliwa."
sw.R: Lakini ninyi mnalitendea jina {{deity_pronoun:langu|Langu}} kana kwamba si takatifu. \q Mnasema, "Madhabahu ya Bwana ni najisi, \q na chakula kinachotolewa juu yake hakistahili heshima."

ko.L: 그러나 너희는 그것을 더럽히고 있다. \q 너희가 "주님의 상은 더러워졌고, \q 그 열매, 곧 그 음식은 하찮다" 하고 말하기 때문이다.
ko.B: 그러나 너희는 내 이름을 더럽힌다. \q 너희가 "주님의 상은 더러워졌고, \q 그 위에 놓인 음식은 업신여겨도 된다" 하고 말하기 때문이다.
ko.R: 그러나 너희는 내 이름을 거룩하지 않은 것처럼 대한다. \q 너희는 "주님의 제단은 깨끗하지 않다. \q 그 위에 바친 음식은 존중할 가치가 없다" 하고 말한다.

decisions.choice: profaning it: profaning the LORD's name
decisions.reason: "It" is the name the nations honor (verse 11). To profane is to treat what is holy as common. |

decisions.choice: its fruit, its food: what is offered on the altar
decisions.reason: The first word, "its fruit", is rare and may mean the produce brought to the altar, or the priests' share of it. Some think it is a copying slip, written twice. "Its food" explains it.

decisions.choice: the table of the Lord is defiled: as in verse 7
decisions.reason: The charge of verse 7 is repeated. Here the word for the Lord is Adonai, not the divine name. |

decisions.choice: treat my name as if it were not holy (R)
decisions.reason: Readable says what "it" refers to and what profaning means (m1). |

decisions.choice: "el Señor"
decisions.reason: Here the Hebrew has Adonai, so "el Señor" takes no divine_name span, as the English "the Lord".

decisions.choice: "Bwana" for Adonai, with no divine_name span
decisions.reason: Here the Hebrew has "the Lord" (Adonai), not the divine name, so Swahili writes "Bwana", as the English writes "Lord".

decisions.choice: "주님의 상" for the table of Adonai; "{{divine_name:주|야훼}}의 상" in verse 7
decisions.reason: Verse 7 has the divine name and this verse has Adonai (the English "the LORD" against "the Lord"); Korean keeps them apart as "{{divine_name:주|야훼}}" and "주님".

source.text: וַאֲמַרְתֶּם֩ הִנֵּ֨ה מַתְּלָאָ֜ה וְהִפַּחְתֶּ֣ם אוֹת֗וֹ אָמַר֙ יְהוָ֣ה צְבָא֔וֹת וַהֲבֵאתֶ֣ם גָּז֗וּל וְאֶת־הַפִּסֵּ֨חַ֙ וְאֶת־הַ֣חוֹלֶ֔ה וַהֲבֵאתֶ֖ם אֶת־הַמִּנְחָ֑ה הַאֶרְצֶ֥ה אוֹתָ֛הּ מִיֶּדְכֶ֖ם אָמַ֥ר יְהוָֽה׃ס

records.literal_gloss: And you say, Look, what a weariness! And you sniff at it, says Yahweh of hosts; and you bring [what was] stolen and the lame and the sick, and you bring the offering. Will I accept it from your hand? says Yahweh.

en.L: And you say, "Look, what a weariness!" and you sniff at it, says {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} of hosts; \q and you bring what was stolen, and the lame and the sick; \q and you bring the offering! \q Shall I accept it from your hand? says {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.
en.B: You say, "What a burden this is!" and you sniff at it in contempt, says {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} of Armies. \q You bring animals that were stolen, or lame or sick, \q and these you bring as your offering! \q Should I accept that from your hands? says {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.
en.R: You say, "We are so tired of all this!" And you turn up your noses at it, says {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} of Armies. \q You bring animals that were stolen, or lame, or sick, \q and you offer them to {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}! \q Should I accept them from you? says {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.

fr.L: Et vous dites : « Voici, quelle fatigue ! » et vous soufflez dessus [avec mépris], dit {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} des armées ; \q et vous amenez ce qui a été volé, et la boiteuse et la malade ; \q et vous amenez l’offrande ! \q L’accepterai-je de votre main ? dit {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}}.
fr.B: Vous dites : « Quelle corvée ! » et vous la dédaignez d’un souffle méprisant, dit {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} des armées. \q Vous amenez des bêtes volées, boiteuses ou malades, \q et c’est cela que vous apportez en offrande ! \q Devrais-je accepter cela de vos mains ? dit {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}}.
fr.R: Vous dites : « On en a assez de tout ça ! » Et vous levez le nez avec mépris, dit {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} des armées. \q Vous amenez des animaux volés, ou boiteux, ou malades, \q et vous {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} les offrez ! \q Devrais-je les accepter de vous ? dit {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}}.

es.L: Y {{plural_you:dicen|decís}}: «¡He aquí, qué fastidio!», y lo {{plural_you:desprecian|despreciáis}} con un resoplido, dice {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} de los ejércitos; \q y {{plural_you:traen|traéis}} lo robado, y el cojo y el enfermo; \q ¡y {{plural_you:traen|traéis}} [esto como] ofrenda! \q ¿Lo aceptaré yo de {{plural_you:su mano|vuestra mano}}?, dice {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}}.
es.B: {{plural_you:Dicen|Decís}}: «¡Qué carga es esto!», y lo {{plural_you:miran|miráis}} con desprecio, dice {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} de los Ejércitos. \q {{plural_you:Traen|Traéis}} animales robados, cojos o enfermos, \q ¡y eso es lo que {{plural_you:traen|traéis}} como ofrenda! \q ¿Voy a aceptarlo de {{plural_you:sus manos|vuestras manos}}?, dice {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}}.
es.R: {{plural_you:Dicen|Decís}}: «¡Estamos tan cansados de todo esto!». Y lo {{plural_you:miran|miráis}} con desprecio, dice {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} de los Ejércitos. \q {{plural_you:Traen|Traéis}} animales robados, cojos o enfermos, \q ¡y {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} los {{plural_you:ofrecen|ofrecéis}}! \q ¿Debo aceptarlos de {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}}?, dice {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}}.

vi.L: Các ngươi nói: "Kìa, thật là mệt nhọc!" và các ngươi khịt mũi khinh nó, {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} Vạn Quân phán; \q các ngươi đem đến [con vật] bị cướp, con què và con bệnh; \q các ngươi đem đến lễ vật như thế! \q Ta há nhận nó từ tay các ngươi sao? {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} phán.
vi.B: Các ngươi nói: "Thật là một gánh nặng!" và các ngươi khịt mũi khinh dể, {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} Vạn Quân phán. \q Các ngươi đem đến những con vật bị cướp, què hay bệnh, \q và đem những con ấy đến làm lễ vật! \q Lẽ nào {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} lại nhận những thứ ấy từ tay các ngươi? {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} phán.
vi.R: Các ngươi nói: "Chúng ta chán việc này quá rồi!" Rồi các ngươi bĩu môi khinh dể, {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} Vạn Quân phán. \q Các ngươi đem đến những con vật bị cướp, hoặc què, hoặc bệnh, \q và dâng chúng cho {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}}! \q Lẽ nào {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} lại nhận chúng từ các ngươi? {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} phán.

sw.L: Tena mnasema, "Tazama, ni uchovu ulioje!" nanyi mnaibezea, asema {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} wa majeshi; \q nanyi mnaleta kilichonyang'anywa, na kilema na mgonjwa; \q nanyi mnaleta sadaka! \q Je, niipokee kutoka mkononi mwenu? asema {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}.
sw.B: Mnasema, "Huu ni mzigo ulioje!" nanyi mnaibezea kwa dharau, asema {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} wa majeshi. \q Mnaleta wanyama walioibwa, au vilema au wagonjwa, \q na hao ndio mnaowaleta kuwa sadaka yenu! \q Je, niipokee kutoka mikononi mwenu? asema {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}.
sw.R: Mnasema, "Tumechoshwa sana na mambo haya yote!" Nanyi mnaidharau, anasema {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} wa majeshi. \q Mnaleta wanyama walioibwa, au vilema, au wagonjwa, \q na kunitolea hao! \q Je, niwapokee kutoka kwenu? anasema {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}.

ko.L: 너희는 "보라, 얼마나 지겨운 일인가!" 하고 말하며 그것을 코웃음 친다. 만군의 {{divine_name:주|야훼}}가 말한다. \q 너희는 훔친 것과 다리 저는 것과 병든 것을 가져오고, \q 그것을 예물로 가져온다! \q 내가 그것을 너희 손에서 받겠느냐? {{divine_name:주|야훼}}가 말한다.
ko.B: 너희는 "이 얼마나 귀찮은 일인가!" 하고 말하며 그것을 코웃음 친다. 만군의 {{divine_name:주|야훼}}가 말한다. \q 너희는 훔친 짐승이나 다리 저는 짐승이나 병든 짐승을 가져와서, \q 그것을 예물로 바친다! \q 내가 그것을 너희 손에서 받아야 하겠느냐? {{divine_name:주|야훼}}가 말한다.
ko.R: 너희는 "이런 일은 정말 지겹다!" 하고 말하며 코웃음을 친다. 하늘의 군대를 거느린 {{divine_name:주|야훼}}가 말한다. \q 너희는 훔친 짐승이나 다리 저는 짐승이나 병든 짐승을 가져와서, \q 그것을 나에게 바친다! \q 내가 그것을 너희에게서 받아야 하겠느냐? {{divine_name:주|야훼}}가 말한다.

decisions.choice: you sniff at it: you snort at it in contempt
decisions.reason: The verb means to blow or puff. The priests sniff at their duty as at something worthless. |

decisions.choice: at it: at the altar and its service
decisions.reason: Jewish scribal tradition lists this among a few places where the scribes changed a word out of reverence: it says that the original read "you sniff at me" and that "at it" was written instead. The meaning is the same in the end: contempt for the service is contempt for the LORD.

decisions.choice: what was stolen: animals taken by robbery
decisions.reason: The word means taken by force. An animal gained by robbery could not be offered (Leviticus 5:23 in the Hebrew numbering). Some take it as an animal mauled by a wild beast, which also could not be offered (Exodus 22:30).

decisions.choice: animals that were stolen, or lame or sick (B, R)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable add "animals". The priests' words are set in double quotes. |

decisions.choice: "lo desprecian con un resoplido" (L); "lo miran con desprecio" (B, R)
decisions.reason: The verb is a contemptuous snort; L keeps the gesture, B and R the attitude.

source.text: וְאָר֣וּר נוֹכֵ֗ל וְיֵ֤שׁ בְּעֶדְרוֹ֙ זָכָ֔ר וְנֹדֵ֛ר וְזֹבֵ֥חַ מָשְׁחָ֖ת לַֽאדֹנָ֑י כִּי֩ מֶ֨לֶךְ גָּד֜וֹל אָ֗נִי אָמַר֙ יְהוָ֣ה צְבָא֔וֹת וּשְׁמִ֖י נוֹרָ֥א בַגּוֹיִֽם׃

records.literal_gloss: And cursed [is the] cheat, and [there is] in his flock a male, and [he] vows and sacrifices a blemished [one] to [the] Lord; for a great king [am] I, says Yahweh of hosts, and my name [is] feared among the nations.

en.L: Cursed is the cheat who has a male in {{gender:their|his}} flock, \q and vows [it], but sacrifices a blemished [animal] to the Lord; \q for a great King [am] I, says {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} of hosts, \q and {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} name is feared among the nations.
en.B: Cursed is the cheat who has a sound male in {{gender:their|his}} flock and vows to give it, \q but then sacrifices to the Lord an animal with a blemish! \q I am a great King, says {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} of Armies, \q and {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} name is feared among the nations.
en.R: A curse on anyone who cheats like this! They have a good male animal in their flock and promise to give it, \q but then they offer the Lord an animal that has something wrong with it. \q I am a great King, says {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} of Armies, \q and the nations fear {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} name.

fr.L: Maudit soit le tricheur qui a un mâle dans son troupeau, \q et qui fait un vœu, mais sacrifie au Seigneur une [bête] défectueuse ; \q car je [suis] un grand Roi, dit {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} des armées, \q et {{deity_pronoun:mon|Mon}} nom est redouté parmi les nations.
fr.B: Maudit soit le tricheur qui a dans son troupeau un mâle sans défaut, qui promet de le donner, \q et qui sacrifie ensuite au Seigneur une bête qui a un défaut ! \q Car je suis un grand Roi, dit {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} des armées, \q et {{deity_pronoun:mon|Mon}} nom est redouté parmi les nations.
fr.R: Malheur à celui qui triche ainsi ! Il a un bon animal mâle dans son troupeau et il promet de le donner, \q mais ensuite, il offre au Seigneur un animal qui a un défaut. \q Je suis un grand Roi, dit {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} des armées, \q et les nations respectent {{deity_pronoun:mon|Mon}} nom avec crainte.

es.L: Maldito sea el tramposo que tiene un macho en su rebaño, \q y [lo] promete en voto, pero sacrifica al Señor [un animal] con defecto; \q porque yo [soy] gran Rey, dice {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} de los ejércitos, \q y {{deity_pronoun:mi|Mi}} nombre es temido entre las naciones.
es.B: ¡Maldito sea el tramposo que tiene en su rebaño un macho sano y promete darlo, \q pero luego sacrifica al Señor un animal con defecto! \q Yo soy un gran Rey, dice {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} de los Ejércitos, \q y {{deity_pronoun:mi|Mi}} nombre es temido entre las naciones.
es.R: ¡Maldito sea el que hace trampa de esta manera! Tiene un buen animal macho en su rebaño y promete darlo, \q pero luego le ofrece al Señor un animal que tiene algún defecto. \q Yo soy un gran Rey, dice {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} de los Ejércitos, \q y las naciones temen {{deity_pronoun:mi|Mi}} nombre.

vi.L: Đáng rủa thay kẻ gian lận có con đực trong bầy mình, \q đã khấn hứa [nó], nhưng lại dâng con có tì vết cho Chúa; \q vì {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} là Vua lớn, {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} Vạn Quân phán, \q và danh {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} được kính sợ giữa các dân tộc.
vi.B: Đáng rủa thay kẻ gian lận, có con đực lành lặn trong bầy và đã khấn hứa dâng nó, \q nhưng rồi lại dâng cho Chúa một con vật có tì vết! \q Ta là Vua lớn, {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} Vạn Quân phán, \q và danh {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} được kính sợ giữa các dân tộc.
vi.R: Đáng bị nguyền rủa thay kẻ gian lận như thế! Người ấy có con đực tốt trong bầy và đã hứa dâng nó, \q nhưng rồi lại dâng cho Chúa một con vật có tật. \q Ta là Vua lớn, {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} Vạn Quân phán, \q và các dân tộc kính sợ danh {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}}.

sw.L: Amelaaniwa mdanganyifu aliye na dume katika kundi lake, \q naye anaweka nadhiri, lakini anamtolea Bwana dhabihu [mnyama] mwenye kasoro; \q kwa maana mimi [ni] Mfalme mkuu, asema {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} wa majeshi, \q na jina {{deity_pronoun:langu|Langu}} linaogopwa kati ya mataifa.
sw.B: Na alaaniwe mdanganyifu aliye na dume mzima katika kundi lake na kuweka nadhiri ya kumtoa, \q lakini kisha anamtolea Bwana dhabihu mnyama mwenye kasoro! \q Mimi ni Mfalme mkuu, asema {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} wa majeshi, \q na jina {{deity_pronoun:langu|Langu}} linaogopwa kati ya mataifa.
sw.R: Laana iwe juu ya mtu yeyote anayedanganya hivi! Ana mnyama dume mzuri katika kundi lake na kuahidi kumtoa, \q lakini kisha anamtolea Bwana mnyama mwenye kasoro. \q Mimi ni Mfalme mkuu, anasema {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} wa majeshi, \q na mataifa yanaliogopa jina {{deity_pronoun:langu|Langu}}.

ko.L: 자기 양 떼 가운데 수컷이 있어서 서원하고도 흠 있는 것을 주님께 제물로 바치는 사기꾼은 저주를 받는다. \q 나는 큰 왕이기 때문이다. 만군의 {{divine_name:주|야훼}}가 말한다. \q 내 이름은 민족들 가운데서 두려움의 대상이다.
ko.B: 자기 양 떼 가운데 흠 없는 수컷이 있어서 그것을 바치겠다고 서원하고는, \q 흠 있는 짐승을 주님께 제물로 바치는 사기꾼은 저주를 받을 것이다! \q 나는 큰 왕이다. 만군의 {{divine_name:주|야훼}}가 말한다. \q 민족들 가운데서 내 이름은 두려움의 대상이다.
ko.R: 이렇게 속이는 사람은 저주를 받을 것이다! 그는 양 떼 가운데 좋은 수컷이 있어서 그것을 바치겠다고 약속해 놓고는, \q 흠 있는 짐승을 주님께 바친다. \q 나는 큰 왕이다. 하늘의 군대를 거느린 {{divine_name:주|야훼}}가 말한다. \q 민족들이 내 이름을 두려워한다.

decisions.choice: a male, a vow, a blemished animal: a vow paid with a defective animal
decisions.reason: A vow offering had to be a male without defect (Leviticus 22:18-21). The cheat has a good animal but brings a damaged one, keeping the better for himself. |

decisions.choice: I am a great King: the LORD is King over all nations
decisions.reason: "Great king" was a title of the emperors of Assyria and Persia (2 Kings 18:19). The LORD is the great King over all the earth (Psalm 47:3; 95:3), whose name the nations fear (verse 11). He deserves better than the governor of verse 8. |

decisions.choice: feared: held in awe
decisions.reason: The word means "to be feared", awesome, as in Zephaniah 2:11. |

decisions.choice: the Lord (Adonai); King with a capital K; the gender setting for the cheat
decisions.reason: "Lord" stands for Adonai, as the settled wording for this title of God. "King" is capitalized as a title of God. The cheat may be any owner of a flock, so Literal and Balanced use the gender setting and Readable says "anyone ... they". |

decisions.choice: "le tricheur qui a ... dans son troupeau" with no gender span
decisions.reason: French "celui qui", "le tricheur ... son" are generic; the English needs {{gender:their|his}} only for its pronoun.

decisions.choice: "le Seigneur" for Adonai; "un grand Roi", capitalised
decisions.reason: As the English.

decisions.choice: "Rey", capitalized; "su rebaño"
decisions.reason: "King" is capitalized as God's title, as in the English; Spanish "su" covers both readings of the English gender setting, so no span is needed.

decisions.choice: "kundi lake", with no gender span
decisions.reason: "Lake" covers a man or a woman, so the English gender setting has nothing to change in Swahili. Recorded once for Malachi.

decisions.choice: The curse placed after its relative clauses at Literal, so the first two Hebrew lines become one Korean line there
decisions.reason: Korean puts the relative clause before "사기꾼", so the English line break after "flock" cannot fall in the same place at Literal; B and R keep two lines. "자기" and "그" need no gender span.

decisions.choice: "bầy mình" / "người ấy" with no gender span
decisions.reason: Vietnamese "mình" and "người ấy" cover men and women alike.
